subproblem.title: Dilations of cycles with the integer slice property have the integer slice property
subproblem.statement: Hypothesis names: (REP) is the first conjunct of the frozen statement of the DAG theorem dimred_mbl_current_foundations, (MR) is the mass identity of dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (the first conjunct of its conclusion, M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every IMRep R of T in an open U and every open W), and (SL) is the frozen statement of dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds; in exactly this form they are hypotheses of the selected parent dmcbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity. (RU) is the exact frozen statement of the parent's sibling dmcbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq, (CT) = (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) that of dmcbr_measure_convergence_tools, (RECT) that of dmcbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent; whichever are needed appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement. In words: (REP) a current T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, with M_W(T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U has a mass representation (μ, ξ): μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ(W) = M_W(T) for open W, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 provided also M_W(∂T) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U; (MR) M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of T in an open U and open W; (SL) for T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) with admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T and L-Lipschitz f there are currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', ∂A_t = B_t on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W; (RU) an identity ∫ξ₁(ω)dμ₁ = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫ξ₃(ω)dμ₃ between admissible pairs, valid for all test forms on an open U, remains valid with all integrals restricted to any Borel set; (T1) measures μ_j with sup_jμ_j(K) < ∞ on compacts have a subsequence converging to a Radon μ (against C_c, limsup on compacts ≤ μ, liminf on open sets ≥ μ); (T2) if X_j ⇀ X with admissible representations (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ_X, ξ_X), limsup_jμ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) on compacts, f continuous and μ{f = t} = 0, then ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j → ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X; (MM) if Z_j(t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t−h < f < t}) on (a, b) then some measurable g ≥ liminf_jZ_j a.e. on (a, b) has ∫_a^b g ≤ L·liminf_jμ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}); (RECT) a Borel M with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ having approximate tangent spaces Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M with x ↦ p_{Q(x)} Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable is countably n-rectifiable. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω_n = unitBallVolume n, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α for covectors, admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P: μ Borel, finite on compact sets, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e., X(ω) = ∫ξ(x)(ω(x))dμ(x) for every test form. ISP (integer slice property) of Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := dilation a λ y = λ⁻¹(y − a); X' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) is called a dilation of X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) if X'(ω) = λ^{−m}X(ω') for all test m-forms ω, ω' on ℝ^P with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)) for every y. Assume (SL) and (RU). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, n := d+1, a ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and X, X' ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with X' a dilation of X. Suppose ∂X = 0 and X has an admissible representation (μ_X, ξ_X) (μ_X finite on compact sets, ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ_X-a.e. x and all α, X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X for all ω). If X has ISP, then X' has ISP.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (dilation invariance of ISP, parent V4(iii)), with step 1(a), (c), (d) supplied by the sibling dilation_calculus (dc).
1. Notation. η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − a), η⁻¹(y) = a + λy; η is a homeomorphism, a measurable equivalence and λ⁻¹-Lipschitz. For a test form ω, ω∘η is a test form (smooth, tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) compact) and is the unique ω' with ω'(y) = ω(η(y)). Let μ₂ := ofReal(λ^{−n})·η_*μ_X and ξ₂(y) := ξ_X(a + λy).
2. ∂X' = 0. For a test d-form φ, (dc)(2) applied to the pair (φ, φ∘η) gives ∂X'(φ) = λ^{−d}∂X(φ∘η) = 0.
3. (μ₂, ξ₂) is an admissible representation of X'. For compact K, μ₂(K) = λ^{−n}μ_X(η⁻¹(K)) < ∞ (η⁻¹(K) compact). If g is strongly measurable with ξ_X = g μ_X-a.e., then g∘η⁻¹ is strongly measurable and {y : ξ₂(y) ≠ g(η⁻¹(y))} = η({ξ_X ≠ g}) has η_*μ_X-measure μ_X({ξ_X ≠ g}) = 0 (use a measurable null superset), so ξ₂ is μ₂-a.e. strongly measurable; in the same way |ξ₂(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ₂-a.e. y. Finally X'(ω) = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ for all ω by (dc)(4).
4. What must be shown. Let (μ, ξ) be an admissible representation of X', (μ', ξ') one of ∂X', and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz. We show: for L¹-a.e. t, every pair A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(φ) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(φ)dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B integer multiplicity.
5. Slices of X. g := f∘η is Lipschitz with constant L·λ⁻¹ (an NNReal). Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P, k := d, T := X, the admissible representation (μ_X, ξ_X), the admissible representation (0, 0) of ∂X = 0 (∂X(φ) = 0 = ∫0 d0), f := g: there are A_X(t) ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), B_X(t) ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A_X(t)(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X and B_X(t)(φ) = ∫_{g<t}0 d0 = 0 for all t, ω, φ; so B_X(t) = 0.
6. ISP of X, instantiated with (μ_X, ξ_X), (0, 0) and g: there is an L¹-null set N such that for t ∉ N and all A₁, B₁ with A₁(ω) = ∫_{g<t}ξ_X(ω)dμ_X and B₁(φ) = ∫_{g<t}0 d0, ∂A₁ − B₁ is integer multiplicity. With A₁ := A_X(t), B₁ := B_X(t) = 0: ∂A_X(t) is integer multiplicity for every t ∉ N.
7. A is the dilation of A_X(t). Fix t ∉ N and A, B as in step 4. Apply (RU) with U := ℝ^P, k := n, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ, ξ), (μ₂, ξ₂) from step 3 and (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): all three pairs are admissible and ∫ξ(ω)dμ = X'(ω) = ∫ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ + ∫0 d0 for all ω. With the Borel set {f < t} it gives A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ = ∫_{f<t}ξ₂(ω)dμ₂ for every ω. By the change of variables for the measurable equivalence η (Mathlib setIntegral_map_equiv, needing no integrability) and integral_smul_measure: ∫_{f<t}ξ_X(a + λy)(ω(y))d(λ^{−n}η_*μ_X)(y) = λ^{−n}∫_{η⁻¹{f<t}}ξ_X(x)(ω(η(x)))dμ_X(x) = λ^{−n}∫_{g<t}ξ_X(ω∘η)dμ_X = λ^{−n}A_X(t)(ω∘η). Hence A(ω) = λ^{−n}A_X(t)(ω') whenever ω'(y) = ω(η(y)): A is a dilation of A_X(t).
8. B = 0. Apply (RU) with k := d, (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ', ξ'), (μ₂, ξ₂) = (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): ∫ξ'(φ)dμ' = ∂X'(φ) = 0 = 0 + 0 by step 2. With the Borel set {f < t}: B(φ) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(φ)dμ' = 0 for all φ, so B = 0.
9. Conclusion. By (dc)(2), ∂A is a dilation of ∂A_X(t) (degree d); ∂A_X(t) is integer multiplicity (step 6), so ∂A is integer multiplicity by (dc)(3). Since B = 0, the currents ∂A − B and ∂A agree on every test form, hence are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and ∂A − B is integer multiplicity. This holds for all t ∉ N, so X' has ISP. ∎
